messages:
noah: Quick note from this morning's rollout: tiny interactive calls (seq<=24) show a p50 bump ~10ms after we enabled cross-tenant micro-coalesce. Not a blocker but consistent.

aya: Confirmed in traces. The coalesce probe path does a linear compatibility scan under the pool lock; under modest occupancy that adds ~6-12ms CPU latency.

kyle: That scan is the packing win: it finds cheap joins across lanes and improves token efficiency. The downside is the fastpath penalty.

sam: Two concrete proposals: (A) dedicated tiny lane (no coalesce) with reserve_slots=1, or (B) opportunistic coalesce that fast-fails if deadline_hint < 8ms.

noah: Both sound viable. Dedicated lane is simple but fragments capacity and may reduce KV-cache locality. Opportunistic path preserves packing but complicates admission.

aya: We should measure per-queue kv_cache_hit_rate and lane_locality. If tiny lane loses >5% cache hit we lose packing benefits.

kyle: Implementation notes: add metric scheduler.microcoalesce.scan_ms, scheduler.lane.tiny.reserved_slots, runtime.queue.kv_cache_hit_by_lane. Also tag traces with prefer_fastpath=true when callers pass a tight deadline.

sam: Short-term mitigation: short-circuit the scan for seq<=24 with a log marker coalesce_shortcircuit=true and enable on 10% of canary pools. Collect 24h.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for pool-micro-canary at 05:40 UTC. Automated thresholds: p50 delta <=12ms, p95 delta <=25ms.

aya: Action owners: kyle -> metrics + reserved_slots flag; sam -> short-circuit patch + log marker; noah -> canary config + experiment matrix; i'll draft the follow-up RFC fragment capturing tradeoffs and success criteria.

noah: Nice. Focus the RFC on measurable gates: p50/p95 deltas, kv_cache_hit_by_lane, fastpath_quota_utilization. Reconvene after 24h to pick between isolation vs opportunistic fast-fail.
